title: VT Level 2 Practice Questions 2026: Free 30-Question Mock Exam
metaDescription: Free VT Level II mock exam: 30 original visual testing questions with answers on lighting, remote viewing, weld gauges, weld discontinuities and codes.
h1: Visual Testing (VT) Level II Practice Questions
intro: These 30 questions are original study questions written by Atlantis NDT for technicians preparing for Visual Testing (VT) Level II. They are not ASNT examination questions and do not reproduce any certification exam.

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2024 edition), the employer certifies Level II personnel after general, specific and practical examinations set out in its written practice. ASNT also offers central ASNT NDT Level II examinations (general and method exams), and employers still carry out the vision, practical and job-specific examinations. This set is pitched at what a Level II must do: set up and verify lighting and equipment, carry out direct and remote examinations, measure and evaluate conditions against a procedure, and report the results.

The questions cover vision and lighting, direct and remote viewing equipment, measurement and weld gauges, weld and material discontinuities, procedures and documentation, and examination practice. Atlantis NDT runs NDT training year-round, with theory online and practicals in its Practical NDT simulator or in person at the client's own facility.
howToUse: Answer each question before opening the explanation, and note the topic of every question you miss.
Work the lighting and weld-size calculations on paper; the explanations show each step so you can check your method.
Check code references against the edition your procedures and written practice actually use, since requirements can change between editions.
Study your weakest topics, then retake the full set a few days later without notes.

questions.q: Under ASME Section V Article 9, direct visual examination requires access that allows the eye to be placed within what distance of the surface, at an angle not less than what?
questions.explanation: Article 9 describes direct visual examination with the eye within 24 in (600 mm) of the surface at an angle of not less than 30°. Mirrors may be used to improve the viewing angle; otherwise remote visual examination is used.

questions.q: What minimum illumination does ASME Section V Article 9 require at the examination surface?
questions.explanation: Article 9 sets a minimum of 100 fc (1,000 lx) at the examination surface, verified with a light meter or a verified light source. Other codes or contracts may set different values, so the procedure governs.

questions.q: A small lamp gives 1,600 lx at the examination surface from 0.5 m. Treating it as a point source at the same angle, roughly what illumination does it give from 1.0 m, and does that meet a 1,000 lx minimum?
questions.explanation: Illumination from a point source falls with the square of distance: 1,600 × (0.5/1.0)² = 400 lx, which is below 1,000 lx. The lamp must be moved closer or supplementary lighting added, and the level re-verified with a light meter.

questions.q: Which lighting technique best reveals small surface irregularities such as shallow dents, scratches or weld ripple?
options: Light directed straight down, perpendicular to the surface
questions.explanation: Low-angle light casts shadows from small changes in surface height, making surface relief visible. Light perpendicular to the surface tends to flatten surface texture.

questions.q: Glare from a polished, machined surface is preventing a clear view. What is the best first step?
options: Increase the light intensity from the same direction
Record the area as not examined without trying anything else
Change the viewing or lighting angle, or use diffuse lighting
questions.explanation: Mirror-like reflection depends on the angles of the light and the eye, so changing either one, or diffusing the light, usually removes the glare. More light from the same direction makes glare worse.

questions.q: Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, who establishes the vision requirements, such as near-vision acuity and color contrast differentiation, for VT personnel?
options: ASNT, which issues each technician's vision card directly
The employer, through its written practice, using the recommended practice as guidance
The customer, separately for every contract
No vision requirements apply to visual testing
questions.explanation: SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, and the employer's written practice sets the vision tests, their frequency and acceptance, commonly including a Jaeger-type near-vision chart test. Color contrast differentiation matters in VT because many conditions are judged by color or shade.

questions.q: Under ASME Section V Article 9, remote visual examination may be substituted for direct examination provided that:
options: The remote system has a resolution capability at least equivalent to direct visual observation
The customer waives the lighting requirement
A magnifier of at least 10× is used
questions.explanation: Mirrors, borescopes, fiberscopes and cameras are acceptable when they can resolve detail at least as well as direct observation. The procedure demonstration shows that they do.

questions.q: Which instrument is best suited to examining the inside of a curved pipe run through a small access port, with recorded images?
questions.explanation: A flexible, articulating videoscope can follow bends, steer its tip and capture images for the report. A rigid borescope needs a straight line of sight.

questions.q: How is the adequacy of a visual examination procedure typically demonstrated under ASME Section V Article 9?
options: By the examiner resolving a fine line or artificial imperfection on the surface or a similar surface
questions.explanation: Article 9 allows a fine line, an artificial imperfection or a simulated condition on the same or a similar surface to show the examination can detect what it must. The demonstration is recorded and referenced in the procedure.

questions.q: When changing from a 3× to a 10× magnifier, what generally happens?
options: Field of view and depth of field both increase
Field of view increases and depth of field decreases
Field of view becomes smaller and depth of field becomes shallower
questions.explanation: Higher magnification shows a smaller area and keeps a thinner depth in focus, so the magnifier must be held steady at the right distance. This is why low magnification is used for scanning and higher magnification for examining a specific indication.

questions.q: An equal-leg, flat-faced fillet weld in a 90° T-joint has 8 mm legs. What is its theoretical throat?
questions.explanation: For an equal-leg fillet weld at 90°, the theoretical throat is the leg × 0.707: 8 × 0.707 ≈ 5.7 mm. 11.3 mm is leg × √2, the length of the face, not the throat.

questions.q: When a standard fillet weld gauge is used on a concave fillet weld, the weld size is determined from:
options: The width of the weld face
The throat dimension, because the concave face limits the effective size
questions.explanation: For a concave fillet weld the gauge checks the actual throat, from which the size is derived. For a convex fillet weld, the size is determined by the shorter leg.

questions.q: Which tool is normally used to measure the depth of undercut?
options: An undercut gauge or dial depth gauge
questions.explanation: An undercut gauge or dial depth gauge measures depth below the adjacent base metal surface. Fillet gauges measure leg and throat, and hi-lo gauges measure joint misalignment.

questions.q: What is a hi-lo gauge used for?
options: Measuring internal misalignment between pipe ends at fit-up
questions.explanation: A hi-lo gauge checks how far the inside surfaces of mating pipes are offset, which affects root quality. It is used at fit-up, before welding starts.

questions.q: On a butt weld between plates whose surfaces are flush, the reinforcement height is measured:
options: From the root face to the weld face
From the plane of the adjacent base metal surface to the highest point of the weld face
Across the width of the weld face
From the weld toe to the fusion line
questions.explanation: Reinforcement is weld metal above the base metal surface, so it is measured from that surface to the highest point of the face. The allowable limit comes from the applicable code or procedure.

questions.q: Undercut is best described as:
options: Weld metal that overflows onto the base metal without fusing
Excess weld metal above the plate surface
A groove melted into the base metal next to the weld toe or root and left unfilled
A crack at the end of a weld bead
questions.explanation: Undercut reduces base metal thickness at the toe and creates a notch. Weld metal that overflows without fusing is overlap.

questions.q: Weld metal that protrudes beyond the weld toe without fusing to the base metal is called:
questions.explanation: Overlap creates a notch at the toe where unfused metal sits on the surface. Underfill is a weld face or root surface below the adjacent base metal surface.

questions.q: Star-shaped cracks at the end of a weld bead are most likely:
options: Hydrogen cracks in the base metal far from the weld
questions.explanation: Crater cracks form when the weld pool at a bead termination solidifies and shrinks, often in a star pattern. Good crater-filling technique reduces them.

questions.q: Viewing the root side of an open-root single-V pipe weld, the original square edges of the root faces are visible along part of the joint. This is:
questions.explanation: Visible unmelted root faces show the weld did not penetrate through the joint thickness. Root concavity is a fused but sunken root surface, and burn-through is a hole melted through the root.

questions.q: Why are arc strikes outside the weld area a concern on hardenable steels?
options: Rapid heating and cooling can form hard, brittle zones and cracks
questions.explanation: An arc strike melts a small spot that cools very quickly, which can produce a hard microstructure and cracking that may start a failure. Codes usually require arc strikes to be removed or evaluated.

questions.q: Why is excessive weld reinforcement with an abrupt toe angle a concern?
options: It changes the weld's chemical composition
It concentrates stress at the toe, which can reduce fatigue life
questions.explanation: A tall cap with a sharp angle at the toe raises the local stress, a key factor in fatigue cracking under cyclic loading. Codes therefore limit reinforcement height and may require a smooth transition.

questions.q: Small, deep cavities on a surface, with the surrounding surface largely unaffected, are most typical of:
options: Erosion that leaves a long, smooth groove
questions.explanation: Pitting is localized attack that penetrates deeply while the surrounding surface stays nearly intact, so pit depth matters more than its surface size. General corrosion thins a broad area evenly.

questions.q: When VT is performed to ASME Section V Article 9, where do the acceptance criteria come from?
options: The referencing code section or contract, such as the construction code
questions.explanation: Article 9 sets how the examination is done, while acceptance standards are specified by the referencing code section or contract. The procedure states which criteria apply.

questions.q: In AWS D1.1, visual acceptance limits for discontinuities such as undercut depend on:
options: The type of connection, such as statically or cyclically loaded, and factors such as material thickness
questions.explanation: D1.1's visual inspection acceptance criteria set different limits for statically loaded, cyclically loaded and tubular connections, and undercut limits also depend on thickness and stress direction. The contract documents determine which category applies.

questions.q: Which standard covers visual testing of fusion-welded joints?
questions.explanation: ISO 17637 covers visual testing of fusion-welded joints. ISO 9934-1 covers magnetic particle testing, ISO 3452-1 penetrant testing and ISO 17636-1 radiographic testing of welds.

questions.q: Which information should a VT report normally include?
options: Only the accept or reject decision

The item and area examined, the procedure, the direct or remote technique and equipment, lighting verification, indications with location and size, the acceptance criteria, the result and the examiner's identity and date
The welder's personal opinion of the weld
questions.explanation: A complete report shows what was examined, how, and against which criteria, so the result can be traced and audited. The referencing code or contract may add specific items.
questions.ref: General VT practice; ASME BPVC Section V, Article 9

questions.q: When photographing an indication for a VT report, good practice is to:
options: Include a scale or reference and identify the location and orientation
Zoom in so only the indication fills the frame, with no reference points
Point a flash straight at a shiny surface
Edit the image to make the indication clearer
questions.explanation: A scale and location reference let a reviewer judge size and find the indication again. Editing the image or removing context weakens it as a record.

questions.q: Which is a typical visual check before welding starts?
options: Joint fit-up: groove angle, root opening, alignment and cleanliness
questions.explanation: VT before welding confirms the joint is prepared and fitted as the procedure requires, which prevents many welding defects. Reinforcement and crater checks happen after welding.

questions.q: Why should slag and heavy spatter be removed before final visual examination of a weld?
options: They are needed for the light meter reading
They can hide surface discontinuities such as cracks, porosity and undercut
questions.explanation: Anything covering the weld surface can conceal discontinuities. The surface condition required for VT is stated in the procedure.

questions.q: During VT of a fillet weld, a fine linear indication at the toe could be a crack. What should the Level II do?
options: Ignore it unless it is longer than the leg size
Grind it out without recording it
Accept it, since VT cannot detect cracks
Record its location and size, evaluate it against the applicable acceptance criteria and report it, requesting supplementary surface examination where the procedure provides for it
questions.explanation: Cracks are rejectable under most weld acceptance criteria, so the indication must be recorded and evaluated, not dismissed or removed without a record. Where VT alone cannot confirm it, PT or MT may be used as the procedure allows.
